LUDWIG Federigan, a climate change and sustainability columnist for The Manila Times’ Green Industries pager, has completed the HERA Extreme Heat Reporting Fellowship in Bangkok, Thailand — joining 20 journalists from across Southeast Asia to strengthen coverage of extreme heat.
The sessions explored heat vulnerability, the unequal impacts of rising temperatures and approaches to reporting that can make those risks clearer to the public.
FELLOWSHIP COMPLETE TMT columnist Ludwig Federigan (standing, second from right) together with all participants of the HERA Extreme Heat Reporting Fellowship in Bangkok, Thailand. PHOTO FROM HERA
Among the speakers were Juthamard Surapongchai of Mahidol University, Atsamon Limsakul of Thailand’s Department of Climate Change and Environment, and Seree Supratid of Rangsit University. Their presentations addressed topics including El Niño, heat-related risks and the region’s climate challenges.
For Federigan, the fellowship offered a chance to build knowledge and reporting skills on an issue with growing consequences across Southeast Asia and to bring those insights to his climate and sustainability coverage for Filipino readers. The fellowship was organized by HERA, which supports journalism on climate and resilience issues.
